clue.text: Cross edge of field?

parts.note: split the answer as a letter, the word or, and a letter: those are the two ends of the word field with a choice between them, which is what an edge of field means

explanation.surface: Someone crosses at the edge of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a clue read backwards: the answer, split up as F OR D, describes either edge of field.
explanation.definitionFit: To ford a river is to cross it by wading through a shallow place.

clue.text: Large quantity of Spooner's urban people

indicators.note: the Oxford don whose tongue swapped the opening noises of neighbouring words, so his version of a phrase trades those sounds

parts.note: urban means belonging to the town; handed the M from the word beside it, that noise is spelt this way
the people here are men; taking the T that town gave up, and letting the vowel slacken, the noise is spelt this way

explanation.surface: Spooner producing his own mangled name for the people who live in towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner clues only open when you say them aloud: town men with its two opening noises traded lands on MOUNTAIN, the second vowel flattening from men to an unstressed ending on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain of washing or paperwork is any daunting heap, so the word covers a large quantity of things that never went near a hill.

clue.text: State I left for job

indicators.note: left here means gone away, so the I is taken out of the verb

parts.note: to posit is to state or put forward

explanation.surface: An official explains that they quit their state job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not the opposite of right: it says I has departed from POSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a position of paid employment, a synonym for a job.

clue.text: Adam didn't have one cut

definitions.meaning: read it as Genesis rather than as a barber's shop: a rib of his was taken to build Eve, so he had none going spare
the butcher's noun, a named joint off the carcass

explanation.surface: Adam is the one man in the shop who declined a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side. Genesis takes a rib out of Adam to make Eve, so of all men he is the one with none to spare; and the butcher sells a spare rib as a cut of pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam didn’t have one → SPARE RIB: his rib went to make Eve, so none was spare. cut → SPARE RIB: a pork cut off the ribcage.

clue.text: Mystery hole

definitions.meaning: the noun: something set as a puzzle to be worked out
read as a verb, to pepper a thing with holes, which is what gunfire does to a door

explanation.surface: An unexplained hole in something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second word is a verb, not a noun: to riddle a door is to shoot it full of holes, which is nothing like the single mysterious hole the surface shows you.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a mystery posed as a question, and to riddle something is to hole it through and through.

clue.text: Had spasms: ill-treated, doc high, cure not right

indicators.note: something ill-treated has been knocked about, and letters knocked about will not stay in the order they were handed over in
right is the crossword letter R, and not is the instruction to leave it behind

parts.note: seven letters of fodder, taken exactly as written
three more, once the R that right stands for has gone

explanation.surface: A patient in a bad way: badly handled, the doctor stoned, the medicine wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical grumble on the surface is doing all the work. Doc high, cure not right reads as a complaint about treatment when it is ten shuffled letters with an eleventh struck out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiccoughs are involuntary spasms of the diaphragm, so a person who has had a bout of them has hiccoughed, past tense to past tense.

clue.text: Fashioned motor van's first edition

parts.note: a motor is a car in everyday British speech

indicators.note: it asks for the letter that starts the word beside it, not for an early print run

parts.note: the opening letter of the word, and nothing more of it
ED is the standard short form on a title page

explanation.surface: The first edition of a magazine about motor vans.
explanation.walkthrough: Fashioned is shaping by hand, not a remark about style, and van's first is one letter rather than an early print run. Two ordinary words, both pulling you the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carved has been fashioned, shaped deliberately out of wood or stone, and both words are past tense.

clue.text: Shock horror, at first express is behind

indicators.note: it puts the second piece after the first, so the clue order is the answer order
it takes only the opening letter of the word in front of it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word, which at first asks for
to air a grievance is to express it

explanation.surface: A tabloid front page: shock, horror, and the express running late.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock horror is a stock tabloid cry, and splitting it is the whole difficulty of a four-letter clue: only the first word defines, and the second belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick tousled mass of it, as in a shock of red hair, so the noun substitutes exactly.

clue.text: Moulding over very old fronts of library offices

indicators.note: it asks for the letter each of the words after it begins with

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's mark for an over
V for very, as in v. good
O for old, the standard short form
the letters those two words start with

explanation.surface: Something moulded lying over the very old frontages of the library offices.
explanation.walkthrough: An ovolo is the fat quarter-round moulding that runs under a cornice, a term from classical architecture rather than the joiner's shop, which is why the bare one-word definition gives so little away.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex quarter-round moulding in classical architecture, so Moulding is the plain noun for the thing itself.

clue.text: New mother, demure, has one jumper

parts.note: prim is demure taken as far as starchiness
the Roman numeral for one
a para is a paratrooper, who jumps for a living

explanation.surface: A shy new mother in a borrowed sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is the trap. The clue is stitched out of clothing words, demure and jumper together, and the one that matters means a soldier who leaves aeroplanes.
explanation.definitionFit: A primipara is the obstetrician's word for a woman bearing her first child, which is New mother in medical dress.

clue.text: Study in location near to you reportedly burning and rendered unusable

indicators.note: it sets the next piece hard up against the one before, which is all a charade ever asks

parts.note: a den is the small room at home where the work gets done
at is the preposition English uses for being in a location

indicators.note: a sound instruction: write down what the word beside it sounds like, not how it is spelt

parts.note: said aloud, the pronoun is a single letter
burning here is a colour, the shade of something red-hot

explanation.surface: A study somewhere close by, reportedly on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: You reportedly is the sound convention worth keeping: said aloud, the pronoun is the letter U. And burning is a colour here, not a fire, which is what the alarming surface is banking on.
explanation.definitionFit: Denatured alcohol has been doctored so it cannot be drunk, so it is rendered unusable for the obvious purpose while remaining alcohol.

clue.text: See 28 Down
Getting French wine, no money left for room

indicators.note: the cancelling word: whatever follows it is struck out of the wordplay instead of added to it
left is what remains, so the word reports the residue after the cut rather than a direction

parts.note: Chambertin is a grand cru red burgundy from the Cote de Nuits
tin is old British slang for cash, and it is the chunk that goes

explanation.surface: Buying French wine has left nothing over for the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Left is the pivot: it means what remains, so the wine gives up three letters rather than turning in any direction. TIN for money is Victorian slang the crossword has never let go of.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room in the grander register, the one used for a council chamber or a chamber of commerce.

clue.text: Irish poet and Unesco luminary discovered

indicators.note: to discover a thing is to uncover what was already sitting there, which is what this run of letters needs

parts.note: the letters run on straight across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A distinguished figure at Unesco turns out to write verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Padraic Colum was a poet of the Irish Literary Revival and a contemporary of Yeats, and his name straddles the join between two words that have nothing to do with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Padraic Colum, 1881 to 1972, was an Irish poet of the Literary Revival, so the definition names him by nationality and trade.

clue.text: Stripy birds, say, or marsupials

indicators.note: say means the word for stripy is spoken, giving only its sound

parts.note: bandy, in the sense of banded or striped, said aloud
coots are water birds

explanation.surface: Some striped birds, perhaps, or else pouched mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like it means for example, but it signals a sound-alike of BANDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandicoots are small insect-eating marsupials of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Revolutionary travelled around Cuba, a country in the Americas

indicators.note: around means the turned word wraps the Cuban letters
revolutionary means turning, so the word for travelled is read backwards

parts.note: rode means travelled, on a horse or in a vehicle
CU is the internet country code for Cuba

explanation.surface: A revolutionary like Che toured Cuba and another Latin American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests Che or Castro, but it signals EDOR, which goes around CU and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American republic, so it is one of the nations of the Americas.

clue.text: See 26
Skirt has Northern material

parts.note: to skirt a field is to run along its edge, and to line a route is to do the same
N is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A skirt run up in cloth from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Skirt is the verb, not the garment: a hedge skirts a field the way a crowd lines a street. The clothing sense is there to keep you looking in the wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is cloth woven from flax, so material is the plain noun for the stuff rather than for anything made of it.

clue.text: Old monk, lacking energy, got the sack

indicators.note: what comes after it is missing from the word, so the letter it names is the one struck out

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was a Northumbrian monk and chronicler of the eighth century
E is the physics symbol, and here it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: An elderly monk, out of puff, is dismissed from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: Got the sack reads as dismissal and means turning in for the night: hitting the sack. Bede, the Venerable, wrote the first history of the English church, which is why a crossword calls him an old monk.
explanation.definitionFit: The sack is old slang for bed, as in hitting the sack, so the definition is an idiom rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Rodri in Paris perhaps knocking back a few

indicators.note: it marks Paris as standing in for French generally, so the word beside it is to be translated rather than used as it is

parts.note: the insides of the footballer's name, once the R, O and I wrapped round them are taken off
where those two letters sit inside that name, and the answer spells the little word out
the R, O and I round the outside spell ROI, and this is what a Parisian means by it

explanation.surface: Rodri out in Paris, celebrating with a drink or two.
explanation.walkthrough: RODRI is DR sitting inside ROI, and ROI is the Paris word for a king. Say the same arrangement in English, DR in king, and the letters are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking back a few is the pub idiom for drinking, so the definition is a whole phrase standing in for the gerund rather than a single synonym.

clue.text: That man will love getting to say this when meeting

definitions.note: The answer is a greeting, not a verb phrase, so the definition points at it rather than substituting for it: this is the word you say.

parts.note: the pronoun standing in for a man already named
he will contracts to he'll, and the contraction hands over its two letters
love is nothing on a tennis scoreboard, and nothing is written as a nought

explanation.surface: A man looking forward to greeting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading that man will as he'll is the move here: apostrophes vanish in cryptic wordplay, so a contraction gives up its letters exactly as if it were a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the standard English greeting, so the clue defines it by the job it does rather than by any synonym for it.

clue.text: Means of escape, quietly opening toilet shack

indicators.note: to open a thing is to cut a gap in it, and the letter named beside it is let into that gap

parts.note: loo is the everyday British word for a lavatory
a hole is the contemptuous word for a miserable little dwelling
P is piano on a score, the musician's mark for playing softly

explanation.surface: Someone slipping quietly out through the door of an outdoor privy.
explanation.walkthrough: A loophole was once a literal narrow opening in a wall, which is why the escape sense and the word hole sit so comfortably in the same eight letters. The privy is the setter enjoying himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap in a rule that lets somebody out of it, so Means of escape is the figurative sense, not a fire exit.

clue.text: Mother's pet breed

parts.note: ma is mother, and the possessive S comes along with her
a pet is a fit of sulks, as in being in a pet, and a tiff is the same thing

explanation.surface: The dog that belongs to somebody's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet is the trap, sitting next to Mother's in a clue that turns out to be about a dog. It is not an animal here but a sulk, the sense that survives in being in a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Breed defines a mastiff the way bird defines a robin, by naming the category and leaving the enumeration and the crossings to narrow it.

clue.text: Kite's one, replacing earlier English model

indicators.note: it swaps one letter for another in a word already built, rather than adding anything to it
the word has two of the letter being displaced, and this picks the first of them

parts.note: Kite is the name at the top of this puzzle, and what Kite is, is one of those
E is the standard short form, and here it is the letter displaced
the Roman numeral, and the letter that moves into the vacated slot

explanation.surface: Trading in an older English model kite for a newer one.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters sign their puzzles, so Kite's one is the byline pointing back at itself. That self-reference is a Guardian habit worth watching for, and the E that goes is the first of the word's two.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is the person a portrait painter works from, so model is the studio sense of the word rather than the catwalk or the kit one.

clue.text: Guy, the Spanish Casanova, pulled up trousers

indicators.note: trousers is a verb here, meaning pockets, so the reversed word takes the article inside it
pulled up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a wolf is a predatory womaniser, like Casanova
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish Casanova hitches up his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a noun but is the containment verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow and guy are both informal words for a man.

clue.text: Not out of Tamarindo or soda bottles?

indicators.note: to bottle a thing is to keep it shut in, which is what these words are doing with a run of letters

parts.note: the run carries on across two word gaps without a break, so the work is spotting where it starts

explanation.surface: Someone taking stock behind the bar: no tamarindo left, no soda either.
explanation.walkthrough: Not out wants to be the cricket phrase and is only its literal self, the opposite of outside. The capital on Tamarindo makes it look like a place that matters, when it is there for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoors simply is not out, inside the building, and the clue trades on you reading not out as the batsman's phrase first.

clue.text: Picasso's uncle follows artist in relationship

indicators.note: it puts the piece named before it after the one named next, so the reading order flips

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's standard artist
tio is Spanish for uncle, and Picasso is there to tell you which language to reach for

explanation.surface: Picasso's uncle trailing along behind a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Picasso is not the artist in the wordplay at all. He is the flag that says the next word will be Spanish, while RA quietly does the painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the relationship between two quantities, three to one and so on, so relationship is the mathematical sense of a common word.

clue.text: Stays around dock, reviewing places to go in New York

definitions.text: places to go in New York

indicators.note: around means the word for stays goes round the turned word

parts.note: rests means stays or remains

indicators.note: reviewing is read as re-viewing, looking back, so the word for dock runs backwards

parts.note: to moor is to dock a boat

explanation.surface: Someone stays near the docks, checking out places to visit in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'places to go' is the euphemism: in American English restrooms are public toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrooms is the American euphemism for public lavatories, the places one goes to relieve oneself.

clue.text: Hake, not initially hunted, loathe swimming in Californian water

indicators.note: swimming means the letters move about freely into a new order
not means the following letter is removed from the fish's name
initially picks the first letter of the word hunted

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A hake that has escaped capture loathes swimming in Californian waters.
explanation.walkthrough: Hake without the first letter of hunted is AKE, which is mixed with LOATHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is the large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the California-Nevada border.

clue.text: Having returned, throw out wrapper for Trump's 'super bad' photo here?

definitions.note: a definition by example, the question mark marking it as one magazine instance

indicators.note: having returned means the word for throw out is turned back to front

parts.note: to emit is to throw out or give off
a cover is a wrapper

explanation.surface: A wrapper is discarded and brought back for Trump's unflattering photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Trump calling a Time magazine cover photo of him 'super bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Time cover is the front page of Time magazine, where the photograph Trump disliked appeared.

clue.text: Blackboard turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry a word turned up is read from the bottom, so it arrives reversed

parts.note: only the back half of the single word is wordplay: to board somewhere is to lodge there, to live there, and that word climbs back up the entry

explanation.surface: A blackboard arriving at the school.
explanation.walkthrough: One word is doing two jobs. Blackboard is split down the middle, Black defining and board supplying the letters, and running two elements into a single word is a favourite way of hiding the seam.
explanation.definitionFit: Black in the moral sense, a black deed or a black heart, is wickedness, which is what the answer names as a noun or an adjective.

clue.text: Vegetable growth after small tank's opening, introducing discharged fluid

indicators.note: after says the growth word comes after the rest
introducing means the fluid word is brought in between the two letters

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of tank's

parts.note: its first letter
wee is informal for urine, a discharged fluid
corn is a crop, something grown

explanation.surface: A plant grows after fluid leaks from a little tank's outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: S and T enclose WEE to give SWEET, then CORN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetcorn is maize grown for its sweet kernels and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Duchess's place bad, even though set back

indicators.note: an across entry runs left to right, so a word set back in one is written the other way

parts.note: mal is the prefix English borrowed for bad, as in malpractice
even though is IF, turned about by the instruction after it

explanation.surface: The duchess's house is in poor shape, though it does stand well back.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duchess of Malfi is Webster's tragedy, so the place belongs to her by title. Malfi is Amalfi on the Italian coast, and the play is the only reason the name is known at all in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Malfi is the dukedom of the heroine of Webster's tragedy, so a duchess's place names it the way Windsor names a castle.
